```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: !expr has_data
# Data-dependent sentences, each with a branch for the other outcome
adjusted_covariates <- strsplit(results$adjusted$covariates, ", ")[[1]]
s_sample <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "All %d patients in the file are described here, in the arm they were",
    "randomized to: %d sugar water and %d licorice."
  ),
  results$n_patients, results$n_by_arm[["Sugar water"]], results$n_by_arm[["Licorice"]]
)
s_complete <- if (results$baseline_missing_n == 0) {
  "No baseline value is missing."
} else {
  sprintf("%d baseline values are missing; percentages use the patients with a value.",
          results$baseline_missing_n)
}
s_preop <- if ("preop_sore_throat" %in% adjusted_covariates) {
  sprintf(
    paste(
      "%d patients had a sore throat before surgery, at least ten, so by the plan's",
      "rule the variable is in the adjusted model (D-011)."
    ),
    results$preop_sore_throat_n
  )
} else {
  sprintf(
    paste(
      "Only %d patients had a sore throat before surgery. That is fewer than ten, so",
      "by the plan's rule the variable is left out of the adjusted model (D-011)."
    ),
    results$preop_sore_throat_n
  )
}
s_merged <- if (length(results$adjusted_merged) == 0) {
  paste(
    "No covariate in the adjusted model has a category with fewer than ten patients,",
    "so no categories are merged (D-016)."
  )
} else {
  sprintf(
    "Sparse categories are merged for: %s (D-016).",
    paste(gsub("_", " ", results$adjusted_merged), collapse = ", ")
  )
}
```

`r if (has_data) s_sample else ""`
`r if (has_data) s_complete else ""`
Continuous variables are shown as mean (SD) and categorical variables as
n (%).

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: !expr has_data
#| tbl-cap: "Baseline characteristics by randomized arm."
labels <- c(
  age = "Age (years)", sex = "Sex", bmi = "Body mass index (kg/m²)",
  asa = "ASA physical status", mallampati = "Mallampati class",
  smoking = "Smoking", preop_sore_throat = "Sore throat before surgery",
  surgery_size = "Surgery size"
)
t1 <- results$baseline
t1$variable <- ifelse(duplicated(t1$variable), "", labels[t1$variable])
knitr::kable(t1, col.names = c("", "", "Sugar water", "Licorice"))
```

Any differences between randomized arms are due to chance, so there are no
significance tests here. Nothing in this table was used to choose
covariates for the adjusted analysis. Those were fixed in the plan
(Chapter 3; D-009), for the reason given in Chapter 4.

Two baseline facts matter for the pre-specified analyses:

- `r if (has_data) s_preop else ""`
  The primary analysis keeps these patients (D-005).
- `r if (has_data) s_merged else ""`
  Mallampati class is not in any model, so the rule does not apply to it.

No models are fitted in this chapter.
